info.name: ZapClaw API
info.description:
Every endpoint of the ZapClaw REST API, generated from its OpenAPI document (version 1.3.0).

Before the first request, open this collection's **Variables** and set `apiKey` (create one in the ZapClaw dashboard under **API Keys**), `from` (one of your connected numbers, E.164 digits) and `to` (a recipient). Every request sends the key in the `X-API-Key` header through the collection's API Key authorization.

Reference: [API and webhook docs](https://zapclaw.app/docs.html?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=whatsapp-api-examples). No account yet: [start free](https://app.zapclaw.app/register?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=whatsapp-api-examples).

Generated by `postman/build-collection.js` in [zapclaw/whatsapp-api-examples](https://github.com/zapclaw/whatsapp-api-examples). Edit the generator, not this file.

## About the API

Public REST API for the ZapClaw WhatsApp gateway. Send WhatsApp text, template, media, sticker, location, contacts, reaction and interactive messages, show typing indicators, mark messages as read, quote messages with replyTo, upload, download and delete media, manage message templates, read and update the business profile, block users, manage QR codes, configure conversational automation, and read message, number and pricing analytics data. Inbound messages, delivery status updates, messages the business sends from the WhatsApp Business app or WhatsApp Web (message.echo, opt-in) and WABA account events are delivered to a webhook URL configured in the ZapClaw dashboard. See https://zapclaw.app/docs.html?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=whatsapp-api-examples for the webhook payload format.

Webhook delivery: a failed delivery is retried 3 times (0s, 30s, 120s). After 20 deliveries in a row have been given up on for the same webhook, ZapClaw stops calling that endpoint, but keeps recording every event with its full payload as a pending delivery, replayable from the dashboard, so nothing is lost. Delivery resumes on the first attempt that succeeds. Account events are delivered even while a webhook is in that state, and the account owner is emailed once when it happens.

Free plan limit: above 500 messages a month, a free account keeps receiving and storing messages, but its message events (message.received, message.echo) are held instead of sent to the webhook. They are recorded with their full payload, marked heldReason "plan_limit" in the dashboard's delivery log, and a resend of one answers 402 held_by_plan_limit. Status and account events are still delivered. Held messages are also left out of GET /api/v1/send/messages. In the minutes after the account subscribes, the last 48 hours are delivered on their own and older ones can be resent from the dashboard. Paid plans are never held.

Coexistence limitations: numbers run in Meta Coexistence (Coex) mode. Throughput is fixed at 20 messages per second regardless of messaging tier, a Meta limit on Coexistence numbers that cannot be raised. Messages a business sends from WhatsApp for Windows or WearOS do not generate webhooks (an unavoidable data gap). Voice/video calls, the Official Business Account green badge (OBA), and ephemeral, view-once and group messages are not supported.

header.description: A value you choose that identifies this send. Repeating the same request with the same key inside 10 minutes returns the first call's answer instead of sending a second message, with an `Idempotency-Replayed: true` header on the replay. Generate it once, before the first attempt, and reuse it on every retry. Omitting it changes nothing. In Postman, {{$guid}} makes a new key on every send. To be able to retry one send without a duplicate, replace it with a fixed value before the first attempt and keep that value for the retries.

item.name: Media
item.description: Upload, download and delete media files

formdata.description: A connected WhatsApp number, E.164 digits.

request.description: Uploads a file and returns a `media_id` handle that can be sent with POST /api/v1/send/media. Per-type size caps: image 5 MB, video 16 MB, audio 16 MB, document 100 MB.

variable.description: The media id of a received media message.

request.description:
Downloads the bytes of media received on an inbound WhatsApp message. The response is the raw file streamed with the correct `Content-Type`. Use the `media_url` provided in the `message.received` webhook payload, which points at this endpoint.

Retry policy: treat `404` as temporary and `410` as final; on `429` and `503` wait the seconds in `Retry-After`. Media stays downloadable for as long as Meta keeps it (about 30 days), including after the message itself has passed your plan's log retention window.

Documents download as attachments with `Content-Disposition` per RFC 6266: `filename` holds an ASCII fallback and `filename*` the exact name, UTF-8 encoded. Other media types are served `inline`.

variable.description: The media id returned by POST /api/v1/media.

request.description: Deletes a media file uploaded to Meta with POST /api/v1/media. Uploaded media also expires on Meta's side automatically after about 30 days.

query.description: Select which connected number's templates to return (E.164).

request.description: List approved templates

Creates a message template and submits it to Meta for review. A newly
created template is not sendable until Meta approves it.

Describe the template with the high-level fields below and ZapClaw
builds Meta's `components` array for you, including the example shapes
Meta requires, which differ by parameter format and are easy to get
wrong.

Alternatively, pass `components` directly in Meta's own format to bypass
the builder entirely. That is the original behaviour of this endpoint and
remains supported; when `components` is present every field below except
`name`, `category` and `language` is ignored.

**AUTHENTICATION templates are different.** Meta owns their structure, so
do not send `bodyText`, `headerText`, `footerText` or `buttons`; they are
ignored. Configure `codeExpirationMinutes`, `addSecurityRecommendation`
and `otpButtonText`; the body and the OTP button are generated.

The {{1}} and {{2}} in the body are WhatsApp template variables, not Postman variables: leave them as they are, and do not define Postman variables named 1 or 2.

item.name: List templates that can be copied to a number

query.description: The number that would receive the copies.

request.description: Templates that exist on your other connected numbers but not yet on the target one. A template lives per WhatsApp Business Account, so each number needs its own copy: this is what a newly connected number is missing.

Recreates the named templates on the target number's WhatsApp Business
Account, from the copy stored on another of your numbers.

Meta reviews each copy independently, so this returns a per-template
result rather than failing as a whole. A media header is re-uploaded to
the target account: Meta's media handles are single-use and account
scoped, which requires the original source URL to still be on file; a
template created before ZapClaw stored that URL reports an error and must
be recreated by hand.

item.name: Replace a template that is still under review

request.description:
Meta forbids editing a template while its status is PENDING: only
APPROVED, REJECTED and PAUSED templates can be edited. If you can wait,
let the review finish and edit it in place with
`POST /api/v1/send/templates/{id}`, keeping its name. To change it now,
this replaces it with a new template under a new name.

The replacement cannot keep the old name. After a template is deleted,
Meta refuses its name and language for hours even when it was still
PENDING, and for 30 days when it was approved. So `newName` is required
and must differ from
`name`, and anything that sends the template by name has to switch to the
new one.

The new template is submitted first, and the old one is deleted only once
Meta has accepted the replacement, so a refused submission leaves the old
template exactly as it was. Deleting the old one removes every language
under its name.

For an APPROVED template, use `POST /api/v1/send/templates/{id}` instead.

Edits an existing template in place, identified by its Meta template id
(the `id` field returned by GET /api/v1/send/templates). The template
keeps its id and its history, unlike `/templates/recreate`, which
replaces it with a new template under a new name.

Takes the same friendly fields as template creation, so a media header,
an AUTHENTICATION or OTP template, COPY_CODE and dynamic URL buttons,
TTL and named variables are all editable. A raw `components` array is
still accepted and bypasses the builder, as before.

Only the fields you send are changed. Meta replaces a template's
components wholesale, so ZapClaw merges your fields over the ones the
template already has: sending only `bodyText` leaves the header, the
footer and the buttons exactly as they were. To remove a field, send it
as `null`.

What Meta does and does not allow:

- Editable only while the template is APPROVED, REJECTED or PAUSED. A
  PENDING one answers 409 with code `TEMPLATE_IN_REVIEW`, and repeating
  the request will not change that. Wait for the review to finish (poll
  GET /api/v1/send/templates or watch the
  `account.message_template_status_update` webhook), or replace it under
  a new name with `POST /api/v1/send/templates/recreate`. Never delete it
  to reuse the name.
- An approved template can be edited once per 24 hours and 10 times per
  30 days. Rejected and paused templates are unlimited.
- `name` and `language` cannot be changed at all. Sending a different
  value answers 400.
- `category` can only be changed while the template is REJECTED, where
  it is the fix for an INCORRECT_CATEGORY rejection. It is ignored on an
  approved or paused template.

Editing an approved template does not send it back to review: Meta
re-approves it automatically unless it fails. ZapClaw reads the status
back from Meta after the edit rather than assuming one.

The {{1}} and {{2}} in the body are WhatsApp template variables, not Postman variables: leave them as they are, and do not define Postman variables named 1 or 2.

variable.description: The template name. The path segment is the template name, not the Meta template id.

request.description:
Deletes a template by its name, in every language it has.

The name is not free afterwards: Meta refuses a new template with the
same name and language for hours even if the deleted one was PENDING,
and for 30 days if it was approved. Never delete a template to
resubmit it under the same name. To change one still in review, use
`POST /api/v1/send/templates/recreate`, which submits the new version
under a new name before deleting the old one.

item.name: Profile
item.description: Read and update the WhatsApp business profile

request.description: Read the business profile
Updates the business profile text fields. Provide at least one field beyond `from`.
Submits a new display name for a connected number. The change is reviewed by Meta before it takes effect.

formdata.description: A connected WhatsApp number, E.164 digits.

request.description: Sets the business profile picture. The image file is capped at 5 MB.

item.name: Block
item.description: Block, unblock and list blocked users

request.description: List blocked users
Blocks one or more users on a connected number. Meta only allows blocking a user who has messaged the business within the last 24 hours.
Unblocks one or more previously blocked users on a connected number.

item.description: Manage QR codes and managed links

request.description: List QR codes
Creates a QR code (managed link) for a connected number.
Delete a QR code
Read conversational automation
Updates the conversational automation config. Provide at least one field beyond `from`.

query.description: Start of the window, a Unix timestamp (epoch seconds).
